pharm: A biodegradable poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) implant injected into the vitreous that slowly releases the potent corticosteroid dexamethasone, suppressing intraocular inflammation, edema, fibrin deposition, capillary leakage, and the migration of inflammatory cells.
quick: 0.7 mg dexamethasone implant injected intravitreally into the affected eye
Limited data; systemic exposure is very low - use only if clearly needed
Systemic levels are very low; caution - decide between nursing and treatment
Intraocular pressure, endophthalmitis signs, lens (cataract), retinal status after each injection
summary: Dexamethasone intravitreal implant (0.7 mg) is a sustained-release corticosteroid delivery system injected into the vitreous through a specialized applicator. It is indicated for macular edema following branch or central retinal vein occlusion, for noninfectious uveitis affecting the posterior segment, and for diabetic macular edema. Dexamethasone suppresses the inflammatory pathways that drive retinal edema and leakage. Because it is a potent corticosteroid delivered locally, the main ocular risks are increased intraocular pressure/glaucoma, cataract progression (in phakic eyes), endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, and implant migration into the anterior chamber (especially in eyes lacking an intact posterior lens capsule). It is contraindicated in active or suspected ocular/periocular infection, advanced glaucoma, and aphakic eyes with torn posterior capsule. Repeat injections are given when benefit wanes.
indications: Macular edema following branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO) or central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO)
Noninfectious uveitis affecting the posterior segment of the eye

dosage.d: One 0.7 mg implant injected into the vitreous of the affected eye
dosage.t: Single injection; repeat as needed when benefit declines
dosage.n: Treat one eye at a time per visit; reinject when retreatment criteria met

dosage.d: One 0.7 mg implant into the affected eye

admin: Administered only by an ophthalmologist experienced in intravitreal injections under aseptic conditions
Apply topical anesthetic and a broad-spectrum microbicide (e.g. povidone-iodine) to the conjunctiva, eyelids, and periocular skin
Inject through the pars plana using the single-use applicator; do not reuse
After injection, monitor for elevation of intraocular pressure and perfusion of the optic nerve head
Instruct the patient to report any symptoms of endophthalmitis (eye pain, redness, photophobia, blurred/decreased vision) without delay
Use caution in eyes without an intact posterior capsule or with an anterior chamber lens - risk of implant migration into the anterior chamber
moa: Dexamethasone is a potent corticosteroid that suppresses inflammation by inhibiting multiple inflammatory cytokines, edema, fibrin deposition, capillary dilation and leakage, leukocyte migration, capillary proliferation, and deposition of collagen and scar formation. It binds glucocorticoid receptors and modulates transcription of pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory mediators (including VEGF and prostaglandins) involved in retinal/macular edema. The biodegradable PLGA implant delivers the drug into the vitreous and retina over months while keeping systemic exposure negligible, providing sustained intraocular anti-inflammatory and anti-permeability effects.

absolute: Active or suspected ocular or periocular infection (viral, including herpes simplex epithelial keratitis, vaccinia, varicella; bacterial; mycobacterial; fungal)
Advanced glaucoma not adequately controlled by medication
Aphakic eyes with rupture of the posterior lens capsule
Eyes with anterior chamber intraocular lens (ACIOL) and rupture of the posterior lens capsule
Known hypersensitivity to dexamethasone or any component
relative: Eyes with a torn or absent posterior capsule (risk of implant migration to anterior chamber)
Pre-existing ocular hypertension or glaucoma (corticosteroid responders)

preg: Adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women have not been conducted with the intravitreal implant. Corticosteroids are teratogenic in animals at systemic doses, but maximum systemic exposure after intravitreal administration is extremely low. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: It is not known whether intravitreal dexamethasone is excreted in human milk, though systemic exposure is very low. Caution should be exercised; a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or forgo treatment, considering the benefit to the mother.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed for renal impairment because systemic exposure following intravitreal administration is negligible.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed for hepatic impairment because systemic exposure following intravitreal administration is negligible.

interactions.food: Not applicable - administered by intravitreal injection.
interactions.alcohol: No relevant interaction with the intravitreal implant.
interactions.diagnostics: No significant systemic laboratory interactions; clinical monitoring is ocular (IOP, fundus examination).

serious: Glaucoma requiring surgery or with optic nerve damage
Implant migration into the anterior chamber (corneal edema, especially in eyes with absent/torn posterior capsule)
rare: Necrotizing retinitis with concurrent ocular infection
emergency: Endophthalmitis (sudden eye pain, redness, photophobia, decreased vision)
Retinal detachment (flashes, floaters, curtain over vision)
Acute severe rise in intraocular pressure
Anterior chamber implant migration with corneal edema

monitoring: Intraocular pressure measured shortly after injection and monitored over follow-up
Examination for endophthalmitis at each visit
Slit-lamp assessment of the lens for cataract progression in phakic eyes
Fundus/retinal examination for detachment and implant position
counsel: After the injection your eye will be monitored for pressure changes; keep your follow-up appointments
Seek care immediately if you develop eye pain, increasing redness, light sensitivity, or worsening or blurred vision - these can signal a serious infection
You may notice floaters or a small red patch on the white of the eye; this usually settles
If you have not had cataract surgery, this treatment can speed up cataract formation over time
Do not rub the eye and follow any instructions about eye drops after the procedure
Report flashes of light or a shadow/curtain across your vision at once (possible retinal detachment)
pk: Anti-inflammatory effect begins within days of injection
Vitreous dexamethasone concentrations peak in the early weeks after implantation
Local release sustained over the implant's biodegradation; systemic plasma levels negligible
Therapeutic effect typically lasts about 3-6 months per implant
Store at room temperature; use the single-use applicator and implant immediately on opening
pearls: Corticosteroid implant - top ocular risks are raised IOP/glaucoma and cataract; check pressure after every injection
Contraindicated in active or suspected ocular infection - steroids worsen infectious endophthalmitis
Implant can migrate into the anterior chamber in eyes without an intact posterior capsule (aphakic + torn capsule, ACIOL) - causing corneal edema
Systemic exposure is negligible, so no renal/hepatic dose changes are needed
Endophthalmitis can occur after any intravitreal injection - counsel on warning symptoms
Effect typically lasts ~3-6 months; retreat when macular edema or inflammation recurs
missed: There is no patient-administered dose to miss; the implant is given by an ophthalmologist. Retreatment is performed at office visits when the clinical effect declines. Keep scheduled follow-up appointments so retreatment can be timed appropriately.
overdose: Overdose is not expected with a single 0.7 mg implant. Inadvertent injection of more than one implant or repeat dosing too soon could increase the risk of corticosteroid-related ocular effects, principally elevated intraocular pressure and cataract. Management is supportive with intraocular pressure-lowering therapy and ophthalmic monitoring; the implant is not removable once injected.
